assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on the magic-wavelength idea, trap many atoms in a Lamb-Dicke regime. They reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and enable relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants, and they underpin a coming redefinition of the second. The conceptual step (magic-wavelength trapping) and the instrumental realisation are both clear. As an atomic physicist I find the control of lattice-induced shifts and blackbody and many-body systematics especially convincing.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock and first demonstrated it. Ye's group brought it to the highest accuracy and stability and developed the spin-polarised fermion and many-body clock work. The two-name configuration is natural and avoids a contested third slot. Contributions to the underlying frequency-comb and laser-stabilisation toolchain were separately recognised in 2005.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories (Japan, USA, Europe) have confirmed and surpassed the early results, and the physics is stable. Recognition is timely, and the redefinition of the SI second would strengthen it further.
uncertainties: Hall and Haensch (2005) and Wineland (2012) already recognised neighbouring clock and comb physics, so the committee must judge the incremental novelty.
Several other groups (for example NIST/JILA, PTB, SYRTE) contributed important accuracy milestones that cannot all be credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 observation of a boson at about 125 GeV completed the Standard Model and was a landmark of experimental physics. The precision detectors and the global analysis made it possible. Subsequent coupling measurements support its identification as the Higgs boson.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised the theory. A prize for the discovery must deal with huge collaborations, and the rules allow at most three people. Gianotti (ATLAS spokesperson at the time of discovery), Jenni (ATLAS founding spokesperson) and Virdee (CMS founder and deputy spokesperson) are a plausible but contestable trio. Della Negra is an equally strong claimant and the fourth name cannot be accommodated.
assessment.maturity: The discovery has been confirmed repeatedly by both experiments and by later data, and the interpretation is stable. The timing is late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Credit allocation within the collaborations is intrinsically arbitrary and this is the main obstacle.
Whether the committee would prefer to recognise the detector-building leadership or collaboration spokespersons is a policy question rather than a matter of evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1995 proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and later proposals for atomic quantum simulation provided the blueprint for platforms that are now at the frontier of quantum computing and simulation. The originality is high, and the work opened a field in which experiments have since realised the proposals.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the clear and unambiguous originators, jointly, of the trapped-ion gate and of the optical-lattice and Rydberg simulation proposals. A two-person prize is cleanly supported. Experimental realisations by Wineland, Blatt and others are partly recognised already by the 2012 prize.
assessment.maturity: The proposal has been realised in many laboratories over almost three decades, and the impact is broad. It is mature, if somewhat overlapping with the 2012 and 2022 prizes.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier atomic-physics and quantum-information prizes may lower the case for novelty.
Whether the committee would rather reward theory or an experiment-led trio (for example with experimental ion-trap leaders) is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED reaches the strong-coupling regime between a superconducting qubit and a microwave resonator, giving a controlled platform for quantum information, quantum optics on a chip and microwave quantum sensing. It is the architecture used in leading superconducting processors.
assessment.attribution: Blais supplied the theory proposal with collaborators, Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. This is a reasonable, compact and fair three-person configuration. Credit for the underlying superconducting qubit goes to the 2025 laureates, and Yale colleagues (Devoret) are already recognised, so the allocation needs care.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation, and the technology scales into large commercial devices. Timeliness is good, but the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits has just covered the neighbouring area.
uncertainties: The 2025 prize may be seen as having already covered the key superconducting-circuit conceptual step.
The relative weight of theory (Blais) versus experiment is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator by Kane and Mele opened a vast field of topological band theory, and experimental realisation followed in HgTe. The conceptual novelty is high and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele are the theoretical originators. Molenkamp led the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe wells (with Zhang and collaborators on the theory side). Hasan's 3D topological-insulator work is also important and cannot be included within three names. The competing ordering among Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Hasan, and Molenkamp is a real unresolved question.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups, with decades of follow-up. The field is mature and the 2016 Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz prize covers earlier topological phases, which makes the specific incremental case a judgement call.
uncertainties: Credit overlaps with Bernevig, Hughes and the late Shoucheng Zhang, who may not be eligible.
Four-name list in the longlist means one major contributor must be left out.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum matter, with a new tunable platform for correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the quantitative theoretical prediction, and Jarillo-Herrero's group performed the key experiments, which makes a theory-plus-experiment trio natural. Other groups (for example Cao and Dean's lab) contributed important observations, which complicates the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups reproduce the central phenomena, but the interpretation of the superconductivity and the correlated phases is still under active debate. The field may be a little early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated.
Fair credit among the experimental co-discoverers and the earlier theory of Lopes dos Santos and others is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BB84 protocol and subsequent ideas established secure key distribution protected by quantum physics, and the field drives experiments with satellites and fibre links. The 2022 prize recognised the Bell-test experiments and quantum information science, so this theory side has not yet been addressed directly.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the originators of BB84. Ekert's entanglement-based protocol is also independent and important, but a three-person prize would require careful balancing. I propose the two core originators.
assessment.maturity: Experimental realisations are mature and commercial. Security proofs under practical imperfections continue to be refined. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Ekert's independent contribution would be left out in a two-person configuration.
Quantum information theory has already received partial recognition in 2022.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard models with tunable parameters: the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition, fermionic Hubbard physics, and quantum gas microscopes with single-site resolution. They give a new platform for quantum simulation and many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Greiner and Bloch observed the Mott transition, Esslinger demonstrated the fermionic Mott insulator, Greiner and Bloch developed the microscopes. The theory proposals of Jaksch, Zoller and others are essential, and the longlist includes Cirac and Zoller, who could be awarded separately under B025. Choosing three experimentalists is clear but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Strong, reproduced results, and the field is mature. Whether it is distinct enough from the 2001 BEC prize and the cooling prizes is a matter of judgement.
uncertainties: Overlap with candidates B025 and the earlier BEC and cooling prizes.
Other groups (for example Hulet, Zwierlein, Kuhr, Bakr) have also made central contributions.
